stations.challenge: Rank freedom, money, friendship, recognition and purpose. Defend your top choice.
followUpQuestions: Can success be separated from social recognition?
To what extent is your definition of success really your own?
Can people with very different lives be equally successful?
languageSupport: The key distinction seems to be …
stations.mainQuestion: If nobody could see your achievements, would you still chase the same goals?
stations.stretch: Imagine losing all public recognition for your achievements. What would change?
stations.subtitle: Start by asking what we are really aiming for.
stations.title: What Counts as Success?

stations.challenge: Compare a student who gets excellent marks but hardly sleeps with one who learns slowly but enjoys school.
followUpQuestions: What does a grading system fail to capture?
Would you rather master a subject or achieve top marks?
How could schools assess progress more fairly?
languageSupport: The key distinction seems to be …
stations.mainQuestion: Do excellent grades reliably predict a successful future?
stations.stretch: Design one fairer way to give feedback at school.
stations.subtitle: When achievements become numbers.
stations.title: The Grade Trap

stations.challenge: Your parents offer to pay for university only if they can choose your subject. Negotiate.
followUpQuestions: At what point does parental support become pressure?
Is choosing your own path always a privilege?
How would you negotiate a serious disagreement about your future?
languageSupport: The key distinction seems to be …
stations.mainQuestion: When should you stop trying to meet other people’s expectations?
stations.stretch: Suggest a compromise that respects both independence and responsibility.
stations.subtitle: Expectations from family and other people.
stations.title: Whose Dream Is It?

stations.challenge: Imagine you suddenly see a friend’s scholarship announcement online. Explain your reaction.
followUpQuestions: How does social media distort our view of achievement?
Can comparison be constructive without harming confidence?
How can you resist the feeling of falling behind?
languageSupport: The key distinction seems to be …
stations.mainQuestion: Are we competing with others even when nobody asks us to?
stations.stretch: Invent two habits that make social comparison less harmful.
stations.subtitle: Why does everybody else seem ahead?
stations.title: The Comparison Trap

stations.challenge: A talented student never enters competitions for fear of losing. Give realistic advice.
followUpQuestions: What makes a risk worth taking?
Why does public failure feel different?
Is the claim that failure builds character always true?
languageSupport: The key distinction seems to be …
stations.mainQuestion: Is avoiding failure sometimes worse than failing?
stations.stretch: Discuss when it makes sense to stop trying rather than continue.
stations.subtitle: Mistakes, risk and trying again.
stations.title: The Fear of Failure

stations.challenge: A student sleeps only five hours a night because of clubs and homework. Give them practical advice.
followUpQuestions: Why does society sometimes celebrate overwork?
Where is the boundary between ambition and burnout?
What compromises would you refuse to make?
languageSupport: The key distinction seems to be …
stations.mainQuestion: Is hard work admirable if it leaves no room to enjoy life?
stations.stretch: Propose a school rule that protects students’ well-being.
stations.subtitle: Ambition, rest and exhaustion.
stations.title: Always Busy, Never Enough

stations.challenge: Choose between a meaningful low-paid job and a secure but dull job. Defend the trade-off.
followUpQuestions: How much does financial security affect freedom?
Can a dream job turn into a burden?
How would you weigh meaning, salary and personal time?
languageSupport: The key distinction seems to be …
stations.mainQuestion: Would you accept lower pay for work you genuinely value?
stations.stretch: Describe a third choice and its limitations.
stations.subtitle: Choosing a future without perfect options.
stations.title: Passion or Pay?

stations.challenge: Write a three-line ‘success manifesto’: We refuse to… / We value… / We remember…
followUpQuestions: Why do we celebrate exceptional achievements?
Can the pursuit of excellence become unhealthy?
How would you define a life that is enough?
languageSupport: The key distinction seems to be …
stations.mainQuestion: Is being ordinary and content a legitimate ambition?
stations.stretch: Challenge one unrealistic idea about success in your society.
stations.subtitle: Do we really have to stand out?
stations.title: The Right to Be Ordinary

warmUp.note: If you want: a short activity to start.
warmUp.prompt: Rank freedom, achievement, happiness and security. Defend your ranking and challenge one assumption.

ui.lessonGoal: Defend a viewpoint and respond to alternative perspectives.
ui.levelTip: Choose 5–6 stations. Give examples and counterarguments, and disagree respectfully.

presentation.introduction: Grades. Expectations. Competition. Failure. The future. Who decides what success should look like? Explore the question together, one conversation at a time.
presentation.privacyNotice: You can use fictional examples. Nobody needs to share personal grades, family problems or private experiences.
quickStart: Give a reason or an example.
Ask your partner a follow-up question.
Open the challenge if you need more to discuss.
presentation.subtitle: A conversation, not a test
